newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China-play shares up in HK, following mainland mkts.
newsitem.headline: China-play shares up in HK, following mainland mkts.

text.p: China-related stocks made strong gains in Hong Kong on Wednesday, taking their cue from strength on A-share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen and amid lacklustre sentiment for local blue chips, brokers said.
"The rise is in line with a slight rebound in the Chinese markets," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The H-share index rose 26.70 points, or 2.77 percent, to 989.17 in late trade while major red chips saw solid gains.
Shanghai Industrial rose HK$0.90 to HK$35.60 and China Resources Enterprises gained HK$0.60 to HK$17.20.
"Investors are switching to Chinese firms following their recent correction and especially in the absence of buying incentives in blue chips," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
The Shanghai A-share index rose 3.25 percent to 1,349.527 and the Shenzhen A-share index gained 2.04 percent to 465.67 on Wednesday.
China-listed A-shares are restricted to domestic investors. H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares in China incorporated enterprises.
